words.enDefinition: a conversation in which people with different cultural backgrounds learn from each other

examples.en: Our club held an intercultural dialogue about how students mark the end of term.
examples.zh: 我们社团组织了一场「跨文化对话」，交流同学们怎样纪念学期结束。

examples.en: The intercultural dialogue brought together students who had never taken a class together.
examples.zh: 这场「跨文化对话」让从没一起上过课的同学聚到了一起。

words.zhGloss: 与特定文化密切相关的
words.enDefinition: closely tied to the practices or knowledge shared in one cultural setting
acceptedZhAnswers: 与特定文化密切相关的

examples.en: The joke was culturally specific, so I asked what I was missing.
examples.zh: 这个笑话「依赖特定文化背景」，我就问自己没听懂的是哪一部分。

examples.en: We replaced a culturally specific example with one everyone in the room understood.
examples.zh: 我们把一个「依赖特定文化背景」的例子换成了在场的人都懂的例子。

words.enDefinition: a mention that relies on knowledge of a shared cultural detail

examples.en: I had to look up the cultural reference in the student film.
examples.zh: 学生拍的短片里有个「文化典故」，我得去查一下。

examples.en: My friend caught the cultural reference as soon as the actor named the song.
examples.zh: 演员一说出歌名，我朋友马上就听懂了那个「文化典故」。

words.enDefinition: the shared background that helps people interpret words or actions

examples.en: The note gave enough cultural context to explain why the audience laughed.
examples.zh: 说明提供了足够的「文化语境」，解释观众为什么发笑。

examples.en: We discussed the cultural context before comparing how our families used the phrase.
examples.zh: 我们先谈了「文化语境」，再对比各自家里是怎么用那个说法的。

collocations: interpret something in its cultural context

words.enDefinition: a way of interpreting experiences shaped by one's cultural background

examples.en: I realised I was reading her story through my own cultural lens.
examples.zh: 我意识到，自己在用自己的「文化视角」理解她讲的事。

examples.en: The class looked at the same illustration through more than one cultural lens.
examples.zh: 全班从不止一种「文化视角」看了同一幅插图。

collocations: see something through a cultural lens
look through a different cultural lens

words.enDefinition: a word, expression or action suggesting how to respond in company

examples.en: I missed the social cue when my classmate glanced toward the door.
examples.zh: 同学往门口瞥了一眼，我没看懂那个「社交信号」。

examples.en: Her pause was a social cue I didn't recognise until we talked afterwards.
examples.zh: 她的停顿是个「社交信号」，后来我们聊过我才明白。

words.enDefinition: the direct meaning of words apart from figurative use or implication

examples.en: The literal meaning made sense, but I didn't understand why it was funny.
examples.zh: 「字面意思」是懂了，可我没明白它为什么好笑。

examples.en: I knew the literal meaning of the phrase but missed the warm tone.
examples.zh: 我知道那个说法的「字面意思」，却没听出语气里的亲切。

words.enDefinition: a message suggested indirectly by the way something is expressed

examples.en: I couldn't tell the implied meaning until my friend explained the situation.
examples.zh: 朋友解释当时的情形后，我才听懂「言外之意」。

examples.en: We compared the implied meaning of the same reply in two different conversations.
examples.zh: 我们对比了同一句回复在两段不同对话里的「言外之意」。

words.enDefinition: no longer conveyed when a message is expressed in another language

examples.en: The wordplay was lost in translation, although the basic message came through.
examples.zh: 基本意思传达到了，但双关的趣味「在翻译中丢失了」。

examples.en: Some of the song's warmth was lost in translation for my flatmate.
examples.zh: 室友听了译文后，觉得歌里一部分温暖的感觉「在翻译中丢失了」。

words.enDefinition: having no exact match in another language or setting

examples.en: The term has no direct equivalent in English, so I described its use.
examples.zh: 这个词在英语里「没有直接对应的说法」，所以我解释了它的用法。

examples.en: I found no direct equivalent for the nickname in my first language.
examples.zh: 我在自己的第一语言里没有找到这个昵称「直接对应的说法」。

collocations: no direct equivalent in another language

words.enDefinition: to preserve the original words closely in another language

examples.en: I tried not to translate literally when explaining the joke to my roommate.
examples.zh: 给室友解释笑话时，我尽量不「逐字直译」。

examples.en: The expression sounds harsher if you translate literally from the original message.
examples.zh: 原消息里的那个说法，要是「逐字直译」会显得更尖锐。

collocations: a phrase that's hard to translate literally

words.enDefinition: an expression with a similar meaning without being an exact match

examples.en: My roommate offered a rough equivalent so I could understand the saying.
examples.zh: 为了让我听懂那句俗语，室友举了个「大致对应的说法」。

examples.en: The tutor asked for a rough equivalent in another language we knew.
examples.zh: 导师请我们用自己会的另一种语言举一个「大致对应的说法」。

words.enDefinition: a word or phrase mainly heard in a particular area

examples.en: My classmate explained the local expression after I heard it at the market.
examples.zh: 我在市场听到那个「当地用语」后，同学给我解释了它。

examples.en: I jotted down a local expression the guide used for the afternoon break.
examples.zh: 我记下了向导称呼下午休息时间时用的一个「当地用语」。

words.enDefinition: the way language is used in a particular area

examples.en: The dictionary marked the word as an example of regional usage in English.
examples.zh: 词典把这个词标为英语「地区用法」的一个例子。

examples.en: We compared regional usage after hearing two different words for the same bread.
examples.zh: 我们听见同种面包有两种叫法，就比较了「地区用法」。

words.enDefinition: humour delivered with a serious manner and little obvious emotion

examples.en: I finally caught her dry humour after listening to a few stories.
examples.zh: 听了几个故事后，我终于听懂了她那种「一本正经的幽默」。

examples.en: His dry humour took me by surprise when we first worked together.
examples.zh: 刚开始一起做事时，他那种「一本正经的幽默」让我意外。

words.enDefinition: said playfully although it sounds serious at first

examples.en: I thought she was serious until I realised the comment was tongue-in-cheek.
examples.zh: 我起初以为她是认真的，后来才明白那句话是「故作认真地开玩笑」。

examples.en: Our group rewrote the tongue-in-cheek caption after a visitor misunderstood the poster.
examples.zh: 访客误会了海报，我们就改了那句「故作认真、实则开玩笑」配文。

words.enDefinition: a set of experiences or ideas used to interpret something

examples.en: Her example came from a frame of reference I didn't share yet.
examples.zh: 她的例子来自一种我还不熟悉的「理解问题的参照框架」。

examples.en: The same event made sense once I understood my friend's frame of reference.
examples.zh: 弄懂朋友「理解问题的参照框架」后，我才明白同一件事为何在她看来很合理。

words.enDefinition: the practice of considering a situation from another person's viewpoint

examples.en: Our class used perspective-taking to discuss why the same invitation sounded different to us.
examples.zh: 我们在课上用「换位理解」讨论，为什么大家对同一份邀请的感受不同。

examples.en: The facilitator described perspective-taking as imagining how the new student understood the exchange.
examples.zh: 引导员举例说，「换位理解」是想象新同学会怎么理解刚才的对话。

words.enDefinition: an interpretation or agreement that people have reached together

examples.en: We reached a shared understanding of the joke after each person explained their reaction.
examples.zh: 每个人解释了自己的反应后，我们对那个笑话「形成了共同理解」。

examples.en: The team developed a shared understanding of why the phrase felt too formal.
examples.zh: 小组对那个说法为什么显得太正式「形成了共同理解」。

words.enDefinition: the usual way a person expresses themselves and responds to others

examples.en: I asked what communication style felt most natural for our partner in the project.
examples.zh: 我问合作伙伴，哪种「交流方式」对他来说最自然。

examples.en: My communication style changed when I moved from voice notes to written messages.
examples.zh: 我从发语音改为发文字后，「交流方式」也变了。

words.enDefinition: to decide what a movement used for communicating is meant to imply

examples.en: I didn't know how to interpret a gesture my classmate made at supper.
examples.zh: 吃晚饭时，同学比了个手势，我不知道怎么「理解它的含义」。

examples.en: Our group discussed whether to interpret a gesture differently when the setting changes.
examples.zh: 我们小组讨论了换个场合是否要用不同方式「理解手势的含义」。

collocations: ask how to interpret a gesture

words.enDefinition: the degree to which words state their point without hinting

examples.en: The directness of his reply surprised me until we talked about the wording.
examples.zh: 他的回复那么「直白」，让我吃了一惊，后来我们聊了措辞。

examples.en: We had different ideas about directness when giving feedback on each other's drafts.
examples.zh: 我们对互相改稿时表达该「多直白」有不同想法。

words.enDefinition: a request expressed through a hint rather than a direct instruction

examples.en: I didn't realise her comment about the window was an indirect request.
examples.zh: 我没意识到她提起窗户是在「委婉提出请求」。

examples.en: The tutor asked which line in the dialogue sounded like an indirect request.
examples.zh: 导师问对话中哪一句听起来像「委婉请求」。

words.enDefinition: to ask about something instead of treating a guess as fact

examples.en: I chose to ask rather than assume what my guest meant by the phrase.
examples.zh: 对于客人那句话的意思，我选择「先问清楚再判断」。

examples.en: Our facilitator suggested we ask rather than assume what the unfamiliar picture meant.
examples.zh: 引导员建议，对不熟悉的图像含义要「先问清楚再判断」。

collocations: choose to ask rather than assume
remember to ask rather than assume
learn to ask rather than assume

words.enDefinition: to clarify the background behind something mentioned in a conversation

examples.en: My teammate paused to explain the reference before finishing the story.
examples.zh: 队友停下来「解释提到的典故」，然后才讲完故事。

examples.en: I asked my roommate to explain the reference to an old television show.
examples.zh: 我请室友「解释她提到的那部老电视节目的典故」。

collocations: ask someone to explain the reference
take a moment to explain the reference
explain the reference to a song

words.enDefinition: a joke or effect based on similar sounds or different meanings

examples.en: I missed the play on words because one meaning was new to me.
examples.zh: 我只知道其中一个意思，所以没听懂那个「双关文字游戏」。

examples.en: The tutor explained the play on words in our club's bilingual poster.
examples.zh: 导师解释了社团双语海报上的「双关文字游戏」。

words.zhGloss: 幽默换种语言不一定奏效
words.enDefinition: a comment that jokes may not work in another language or setting
acceptedZhAnswers: 幽默换种语言不一定奏效

examples.en: “Humour doesn't always translate,” my classmate said after trying to explain the pun.
examples.zh: 同学试着解释完双关后说「幽默换种语言不一定奏效」。

examples.en: I said, “Humour doesn't always translate,” when the punchline sounded flat in English.
examples.zh: 笑点译成英语显得平淡时，我说「幽默换种语言不一定奏效」。

words.enDefinition: a variety in how a group of people pronounce their language

examples.en: Our student radio show included a range of accents from across the campus.
examples.zh: 我们的学生广播节目里能听到校园里的「多种口音」。

examples.en: I heard a range of accents in the audio guide made by volunteers.
examples.zh: 志愿者制作的语音导览里，我听到了「多种口音」。

collocations: a recording with a range of accents

words.enDefinition: unfair assumptions based on the way someone pronounces a language

examples.en: The workshop discussed accent bias using feedback from students who had presented projects.
examples.zh: 工作坊用做过项目汇报的同学收到的反馈，讨论了「口音偏见」。

examples.en: We looked at how accent bias can affect whose ideas get noticed.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「口音偏见」如何影响谁的想法能得到关注。

words.enDefinition: to convey the meaning even if the original wording changes

examples.en: I chose to translate the idea rather than keep every word in order.
examples.zh: 我选择「把原意转达出来」，没有按原来的词序逐个词照搬。

examples.en: My friend helped me translate the idea in a way our group understood.
examples.zh: 朋友帮我用小组都听得懂的方式「把原意转达出来」。

collocations: translate the idea into everyday language

words.enDefinition: to imagine extra meaning without enough evidence to support it

examples.en: I tried not to read too much into my classmate's short reply.
examples.zh: 同学回复得很简短，我尽量不「过度解读」。

examples.en: It was easy to read too much into the long pause before her answer.
examples.zh: 她回答前停顿了很久，很容易让人「过度解读」。

collocations: try not to read too much into a remark
read too much into a pause
easy to read too much into a short reply

words.expression: what does that tradition mean to you
words.lemma: what does that tradition mean to you
words.zhGloss: 这个传统对你有什么意义
words.enDefinition: a question asking how a person values a custom they know
acceptedZhAnswers: 这个传统对你有什么意义
acceptedEnVariants: what does that tradition mean to you

examples.en: “What does that tradition mean to you?” my classmate asked during the story circle.
examples.zh: 故事分享会上，同学问我「这个传统对你有什么意义？」

examples.en: I listened to her memories and asked, “What does that tradition mean to you?”
examples.zh: 听她讲完回忆后，我问「这个传统对你有什么意义？」

collocations: ask “What does that tradition mean to you?”
“What does that tradition mean to you personally?”
“What does that tradition mean to you now?”

words.zhGloss: 这个传统是怎么开始的
words.enDefinition: a question about the origins of a particular practice
acceptedZhAnswers: 这个传统是怎么开始的

examples.en: “How did that tradition start?” I asked after hearing about my friend's school.
examples.zh: 听朋友说起以前的学校后，我问「这个传统是怎么开始的？」

examples.en: The volunteer pointed to an old photograph and asked, “How did that tradition start?”
examples.zh: 志愿者指着一张老照片问「这个传统是怎么开始的？」

collocations: “How did that tradition start at your school?”
“How did that tradition start in your family?”

words.enDefinition: a question asking whether a practice is particular to someone's family

examples.en: “Is that a family tradition?” I asked about the meal she had described.
examples.zh: 她描述那顿饭后，我问「那是你家的传统吗？」

examples.en: My roommate asked, “Is that a family tradition?” after hearing about our song.
examples.zh: 听我讲完我们唱的那首歌后，室友问「那是你家的传统吗？」

collocations: “Is that a family tradition for birthdays?”
“Is that a family tradition or something newer?”

words.enDefinition: a question asking if a practice differs between areas

examples.en: “Does it vary by region?” I asked after hearing two names for the bread.
examples.zh: 听到这种面包有两种叫法后，我问「各地叫法一样吗？」

examples.en: Our tutor asked, “Does it vary by region?” when the students compared their stories.
examples.zh: 同学们对比各自讲的事时，导师问「各地做法有差别吗？」

collocations: “Does it vary by region where you live?”

words.expression: what do you call it where you're from
words.lemma: what do you call it where you're from
words.enDefinition: a question asking for the local name of a familiar thing
acceptedEnVariants: what do you call it where you're from

examples.en: I showed my classmate the pastry and asked, “What do you call it where you're from?”
examples.zh: 我把糕点给同学看，问「你们那儿怎么叫它？」

examples.en: “What do you call it where you're from?” the volunteer asked about the game.
examples.zh: 志愿者提到那个游戏时问「你们那儿怎么叫它？」

collocations: ask “What do you call it where you're from?”
“I wonder what you call it where you're from”
“What do people call it where you're from?”

words.enDefinition: in the place where I spent my childhood

examples.en: Where I grew up, the library lent out musical instruments as well as books.
examples.zh: 「在我长大的地方」，图书馆除了书，还借乐器。

examples.en: We had a different name for this game where I grew up.
examples.zh: 「在我长大的地方」，我们管这个游戏叫另一个名字。

words.expression: at my school, we used to
words.lemma: at my school, we used to
words.zhGloss: 在我以前的学校，我们常常
words.enDefinition: a phrase introducing a repeated practice from one's own school
acceptedZhAnswers: 在我以前的学校，我们常常
acceptedEnVariants: at my school, we used to

examples.en: At my school, we used to write notes to the next graduating class.
examples.zh: 「在我以前的学校，我们常常」给下一届毕业生写便条。

examples.en: At my school, we used to spend Friday afternoons showing each other projects.
examples.zh: 「在我以前的学校，我们常常」在周五下午和同学互相展示项目。

collocations: “At my school, we used to share our work”
“At my school, we used to do it differently”
“At my school, we used to start later”

words.enDefinition: an introduction limiting a practice to what one's family normally does

examples.en: In my family, we usually save a small piece of cake for anyone absent.
examples.zh: 「我们家一般会」给没到场的人留一小块蛋糕。

examples.en: In my family, we usually make the cards ourselves before a reunion.
examples.zh: 「我们家一般会」在聚会前自己做卡片。

collocations: “In my family, we usually make it together”
“In my family, we usually keep it simple”
“In my family, we usually celebrate at home”

words.expression: I can't speak for my whole country
words.lemma: i can't speak for my whole country
words.zhGloss: 我不能代表整个国家的人
words.enDefinition: a statement limiting what you say to your own experience
acceptedZhAnswers: 我不能代表整个国家的人
acceptedEnVariants: I can't speak for my whole country

examples.en: I can't speak for my whole country, but my neighbours didn't do that.
examples.zh: 「我不能代表整个国家的人」，不过我以前的邻居不这么做。

examples.en: “I can't speak for my whole country,” she said before describing her own experience.
examples.zh: 她介绍自己的经历前说「我不能代表整个国家的人」。

collocations: say “I can't speak for my whole country”
“I can't speak for my whole country, only my family”
“I can't speak for my whole country on that”

words.expression: that varies from family to family
words.lemma: that varies from family to family
words.enDefinition: a response saying a practice differs between households
acceptedEnVariants: that varies from family to family

examples.en: “That varies from family to family,” I said when asked who usually cooked.
examples.zh: 有人问一般由谁来做饭，我说「各家做法不太一样」。

examples.en: My classmate said, “That varies from family to family,” while discussing birthday meals.
examples.zh: 聊到生日那顿饭时，同学说「各家做法不太一样」。

collocations: say “That varies from family to family”
“I think that varies from family to family”
“That varies from family to family here”

words.enDefinition: a custom shared and maintained within a particular family

examples.en: Making a photo album each year is a family tradition for my roommate.
examples.zh: 室友每年做一本相册，那是他们的「家庭传统」。

examples.en: We wrote down one family tradition each for the class display board.
examples.zh: 我们每人写下一项「家庭传统」，展示在班级展板上。

collocations: a family tradition passed down over time

words.enDefinition: a practice especially associated with a particular area

examples.en: We learned about a regional custom from a student who grew up nearby.
examples.zh: 住在附近长大的一位同学给我们讲了一个「地方习俗」。

examples.en: The display described the game as a regional custom with several local versions.
examples.zh: 展板把这个游戏介绍为一种「地方习俗」，各地玩法略有不同。

collocations: explain the history of a regional custom

words.enDefinition: a repeated activity or way of doing something shared within a cultural setting

examples.en: Our project focused on a cultural practice my neighbour had taught me.
examples.zh: 我们的项目关注我邻居曾教给我的一种「文化惯例」。

examples.en: The volunteer described the cultural practice through examples from her own childhood.
examples.zh: 志愿者用自己童年的例子介绍了这种「文化惯例」。

words.enDefinition: differences among people or settings within a shared cultural background

examples.en: The film showed variation within a culture by following three different households.
examples.zh: 影片拍了三个不同家庭，展示了「同一文化内部的差异」。

examples.en: Our discussion focused on variation within a culture rather than broad national comparisons.
examples.zh: 我们的讨论主要关注「同一文化内部的差异」，少做宽泛的国别比较。

words.enDefinition: to teach or give a custom to a younger generation

examples.en: My friend learned how to pass down a tradition by cooking with her aunt.
examples.zh: 朋友跟姨妈学做菜，明白了怎样「把传统传给后辈」。

examples.en: The film showed how people pass down a tradition through songs and stories.
examples.zh: 影片展示了人们怎样用歌和故事「把传统传给后辈」。

collocations: pass down a tradition through storytelling
decide how to pass down a tradition

words.enDefinition: to continue a custom so it is not forgotten

examples.en: The students wanted to keep a tradition alive by teaching their friends the game.
examples.zh: 同学们想把这个游戏教给朋友，「让传统延续下去」。

examples.en: My aunt records old songs to help keep a tradition alive for our family.
examples.zh: 我姨妈录下老歌，帮助「让家里的传统延续下去」。

collocations: work to keep a tradition alive
aim to keep a tradition alive

words.zhGloss: 恢复一项曾中断的传统
words.enDefinition: to start a customary activity again after it stopped for a time
acceptedZhAnswers: 恢复一项曾中断的传统

examples.en: Our society voted to revive a tradition that had lapsed during remote classes.
examples.zh: 社团表决同意「恢复一项线上上课期间中断的传统」。

examples.en: The neighbours decided to revive a tradition from an old community newsletter.
examples.zh: 邻居们决定「恢复一项曾中断的传统」，灵感来自旧的社区通讯。

collocations: revive a tradition after a pause

words.enDefinition: to combine elements of more than one custom in the same activity

examples.en: My roommates decided to blend traditions when planning their end-of-term dinner together.
examples.zh: 室友们筹划期末聚餐时，决定「把不同传统结合起来」。

examples.en: The students found a way to blend traditions in the decorations for their table.
examples.zh: 同学们想出办法，在餐桌装饰上「把不同传统结合起来」。

words.expression: put your own spin on it
words.lemma: put your own spin on it
words.enDefinition: to change something familiar so it reflects your own ideas
acceptedEnVariants: put your own spin on it

examples.en: My aunt said to put your own spin on it when following her recipe.
examples.zh: 姨妈说，照她的菜谱做时也可以「按自己的方式改一改」。

examples.en: The volunteer said, “Put your own spin on it,” and showed us her version.
examples.zh: 志愿者说「按自己的方式改一改」，然后给我们看了她的版本。

collocations: feel free to put your own spin on it
try to put your own spin on it
find a way to put your own spin on it

words.enDefinition: a statement limiting a familiar practice to one's place of origin

examples.en: “That's specific to my hometown,” I said when someone asked about our procession.
examples.zh: 有人问起我们的游行活动时，我说「那是我家乡才有的」。

examples.en: She explained, “That's specific to my hometown,” after we asked about the lanterns.
examples.zh: 我们问起那些灯笼后，她解释道「那是我家乡才有的」。

collocations: “I think that's specific to my hometown”
“That's specific to my hometown as far as I know”

words.expression: there's no one way to do it
words.lemma: there's no one way to do it
words.enDefinition: a comment recognising that a practice has more than one valid form
acceptedEnVariants: there's no one way to do it

examples.en: “There's no one way to do it,” my friend said during the recipe swap.
examples.zh: 大家交换菜谱时，朋友说「做法不止一种」。

examples.en: The tutor wrote, “There's no one way to do it,” beside the examples.
examples.zh: 导师在这些例子旁写着「做法不止一种」。

collocations: say “There's no one way to do it”
“There's no one way to do it here”
“Remember, there's no one way to do it”

words.zhGloss: 在不同代之间分享故事
words.enDefinition: to tell and listen to accounts among people of different ages
acceptedZhAnswers: 在不同代之间分享故事

examples.en: The library invited families to share stories across generations for its audio archive.
examples.zh: 图书馆请各个家庭「在不同代之间分享故事」，录音会收入档案。

examples.en: The student group used interviews to share stories across generations in their neighbourhood.
examples.zh: 学生小组通过访谈「在社区的不同代之间分享故事」。

collocations: invite people to share stories across generations
a chance to share stories across generations
share stories across generations through interviews

words.enDefinition: to learn about a custom by seeing or experiencing it yourself

examples.en: I wanted to learn about a tradition first-hand by watching my friend prepare the meal.
examples.zh: 我想看朋友准备这顿饭，「亲身了解一项传统」。

examples.en: The exhibit let visitors learn about a tradition first-hand from the people who practise it.
examples.zh: 展览让参观者跟践行这一传统的人交流，「亲身了解一项传统」。

collocations: a chance to learn about a tradition first-hand
help people learn about a tradition first-hand
learn about a tradition first-hand from participants

words.zhGloss: 不是每个人都过这个节
words.enDefinition: a reminder that a celebration is not shared by all people
acceptedZhAnswers: 不是每个人都过这个节

examples.en: “Not everyone celebrates it,” I reminded the club before we made the poster.
examples.zh: 社团做海报之前，我提醒大家「不是每个人都过这个节」。

examples.en: My classmate said, “Not everyone celebrates it,” when asked about our winter break.
examples.zh: 有人问起我们的寒假时，同学说「不是每个人都过这个节」。

words.enDefinition: a statement noting that practices do not always stay the same

examples.en: “Customs change over time,” the speaker said, holding up two old photographs.
examples.zh: 发言者举着两张老照片说「习俗会随时间变化」。

examples.en: We talked about how customs change over time after comparing our family stories.
examples.zh: 对比各家的故事后，我们谈到了「习俗会随时间变化」。

collocations: discuss how customs change over time
show how customs change over time
recognise that customs change over time

words.expression: show me how your family does it
words.lemma: show me how your family does it
words.zhGloss: 给我看看你家是怎么做的
words.enDefinition: a request to demonstrate one's particular family version of an activity
acceptedZhAnswers: 给我看看你家是怎么做的
acceptedEnVariants: show me how your family does it

examples.en: “Could you show me how your family does it?” I asked during the workshop.
examples.zh: 工作坊里，我问「能给我看看你家是怎么做的吗？」

examples.en: I said, “Show me how your family does it,” when she offered a demonstration.
examples.zh: 她提出做示范时，我说「给我看看你家是怎么做的」。

collocations: could you show me how your family does it
please show me how your family does it
ask someone to show me how your family does it

words.expression: do you still do that now
words.lemma: do you still do that now
words.enDefinition: a question asking whether an earlier habit continues into the present
acceptedEnVariants: do you still do that now

examples.en: “Do you still do that now?” I asked after hearing about her childhood meals.
examples.zh: 听她讲完小时候怎么吃饭，我问「你现在还这样做吗？」

examples.en: He described his family's old routine, so I asked, “Do you still do that now?”
examples.zh: 他讲了家里以前的日常做法，我就问「你现在还这样做吗？」

collocations: ask “Do you still do that now?”
“Do you still do that now that you live here?”
“I wonder whether you still do that now”

words.enDefinition: a statement that different practices can continue in the same group

examples.en: Our facilitator said different customs can coexist, even in a single shared kitchen.
examples.zh: 引导员说，即使在同一间共用厨房里，「不同习俗也可以共存」。

examples.en: The photo project showed how different customs can coexist in the same neighbourhood.
examples.zh: 摄影项目展示了「不同习俗怎样在同一社区共存」。

collocations: recognise that different customs can coexist
show how different customs can coexist
find a place where different customs can coexist

words.enDefinition: to continue the practice that has personal or family meaning for you

examples.en: The host explained that you could follow your own tradition at this gathering.
examples.zh: 主持人解释说，在这次聚会上可以「按自己的传统来」。

examples.en: Our club said, “Follow your own tradition if you want to mark the occasion.”
examples.zh: 社团说「想纪念这一天的话，可以按自己的传统来」。

collocations: choose to follow your own tradition
be welcome to follow your own tradition
continue to follow your own tradition

words.enDefinition: to experience something you do not already know

examples.en: A friend encouraged me to try something unfamiliar at the student food fair.
examples.zh: 朋友鼓励我在学生美食节上「尝试不熟悉的食物」。

examples.en: I decided to try something unfamiliar and asked how the game worked.
examples.zh: 我决定「尝试不熟悉的事物」，便问这个游戏怎么玩。

collocations: be willing to try something unfamiliar
have a chance to try something unfamiliar

words.enDefinition: to ask what to do to join an unfamiliar activity

examples.en: I waited for a pause to ask how to take part in the dance.
examples.zh: 我等活动暂停下来，才「问怎么加入这支舞」。

examples.en: My roommate encouraged me to ask how to take part before the workshop began.
examples.zh: 室友鼓励我在工作坊开始前「问一下怎么参加」。

collocations: feel free to ask how to take part
go over to ask how to take part
encourage someone to ask how to take part

words.expression: the version I grew up with
words.lemma: the version i grew up with
words.zhGloss: 我从小熟悉的那个版本
words.enDefinition: the form of a story or practice familiar from childhood
acceptedZhAnswers: 我从小熟悉的那个版本
acceptedEnVariants: the version I grew up with

examples.en: The version I grew up with ends with everyone helping the youngest child.
examples.zh: 「我从小熟悉的那个版本」结尾是大家一起帮助最小的孩子。

examples.en: I learned that the version I grew up with differed from my roommate's.
examples.zh: 我发现，「我从小熟悉的那个版本」和室友知道的不一样。

collocations: tell the version I grew up with
show the version I grew up with
remember the version I grew up with

words.enDefinition: to become comfortable with a repeated pattern of daily activities

examples.en: It took me a few weeks to settle into a routine after moving overseas.
examples.zh: 搬到国外后，我过了几周才「逐渐适应新的日常」。

examples.en: Volunteering on Thursdays helped me settle into a routine during my first term.
examples.zh: 第一学期，每周四做志愿服务帮我「逐渐适应了新的日常」。

collocations: begin to settle into a routine
help someone settle into a routine
settle into a routine after moving

words.enDefinition: the speed and rhythm of ordinary activities in a place

examples.en: The pace of life felt different after I moved out of halls.
examples.zh: 搬出宿舍后，我觉得「生活节奏」变了。

examples.en: My roommate said she preferred the pace of life in her new neighbourhood.
examples.zh: 室友说，她更喜欢新社区的「生活节奏」。

collocations: get used to the pace of life
enjoy the local pace of life

words.expression: take a while to feel settled
words.lemma: take a while to feel settled
words.zhGloss: 过一阵才觉得安顿下来
words.enDefinition: to need some time before feeling comfortable in a new place
acceptedZhAnswers: 过一阵才觉得安顿下来
acceptedEnVariants: take a while to feel settled

examples.en: My roommate said it might take a while to feel settled after the move.
examples.zh: 室友说，搬家后可能「要过一阵才觉得安顿下来」。

examples.en: I told the new student it can take a while to feel settled.
examples.zh: 我告诉新同学，有时「要过一阵才觉得安顿下来」。

collocations: expect it to take a while to feel settled
it may take a while to feel settled
take a while to feel settled after moving

words.enDefinition: to develop regular connections with people in an area

examples.en: I started volunteering to build ties with the community beyond our campus.
examples.zh: 我开始做志愿服务，想「和校外的当地社区建立联系」。

examples.en: The student garden helped us build ties with the community around the university.
examples.zh: 学生花园帮我们「和大学周边的社区建立了联系」。

collocations: volunteer to build ties with the community
help build ties with the community
find ways to build ties with the community

words.enDefinition: to start returning somewhere often enough to be recognised

examples.en: I wanted to become a regular at the neighbourhood repair café that term.
examples.zh: 那一学期，我想「成为社区维修咖啡馆的常客」。

examples.en: It didn't take long to become a regular at the Saturday library group.
examples.zh: 没多久，我就「成了周六图书馆小组的常客」。

collocations: become a regular at a meeting

words.enDefinition: to develop lasting connections with a place where you live

examples.en: I started to put down roots when I joined the neighbourhood choir.
examples.zh: 加入邻里合唱团后，我开始「在当地扎下根」。

examples.en: After graduation, she wanted to put down roots in the city she knew.
examples.zh: 毕业后，她想「在自己熟悉的城市扎下根」。

collocations: put down roots in a new city

words.enDefinition: to maintain contact with the people or customs of where you come from

examples.en: Playing the songs my cousin sends helps me stay connected to home.
examples.zh: 听表亲发来的歌，能帮我「保持与家乡的联系」。

examples.en: Sharing recipes was how our flatmates chose to stay connected to home.
examples.zh: 室友们选择互相分享菜谱，「保持与家乡的联系」。

collocations: find ways to stay connected to home
help someone stay connected to home
stay connected to home while abroad

words.expression: bring a bit of home with me
words.lemma: bring a bit of home with me
words.zhGloss: 把一点家乡的感觉带在身边
words.enDefinition: to take something familiar that makes a new place feel more personal
acceptedZhAnswers: 把一点家乡的感觉带在身边
acceptedEnVariants: bring a bit of home with me

examples.en: I chose a small photo album to bring a bit of home with me.
examples.zh: 我挑了本小相册，「把一点家乡的感觉带在身边」。

examples.en: “I wanted to bring a bit of home with me,” she said, showing her notebook.
examples.zh: 她给大家看了笔记本，说「我想把一点家乡的感觉带在身边」。

collocations: choose to bring a bit of home with me
try to bring a bit of home with me
want to bring a bit of home with me

words.enDefinition: things that make you remember the place or people you come from

examples.en: The smells from my roommate's kitchen were unexpected reminders of home.
examples.zh: 室友厨房里的香味，意外成了「让人想起家乡的事物」。

examples.en: I kept a few reminders of home on the shelf above my bed.
examples.zh: 我把几样「让人想起家乡的事物」放在床上方的架子上。

words.enDefinition: to feel the absence of familiar everyday details

examples.en: I miss the little things, like hearing our neighbours talking in the stairwell.
examples.zh: 我「想念那些小事」，比如听以前的邻居在楼梯间聊天。

examples.en: My classmate said she started to miss the little things after the first month.
examples.zh: 同学说，过了第一个月，她开始「想念那些小事」。

collocations: start to miss the little things
miss the little things about home

words.zhGloss: 在两个选择间左右为难
words.enDefinition: to have conflicting feelings about two people, places or choices
acceptedZhAnswers: 在两个选择间左右为难

examples.en: I sometimes feel torn between spending breaks here and going back home.
examples.zh: 放假的时候，我有时在留在这边和回老家之间「左右为难」。

examples.en: I started to feel torn between keeping my old routines and trying new ones.
examples.zh: 我开始在沿用以前的生活习惯和尝试新习惯之间「左右为难」。

collocations: feel torn between two ways of doing things

words.enDefinition: living with experiences shaped by two cultural settings

examples.en: She wrote about growing up between two cultures in a student magazine.
examples.zh: 她在学生杂志上写了自己「在两种文化之间」长大的经历。

examples.en: I heard different stories about moving between two cultures at the workshop.
examples.zh: 我在工作坊听到不同的人讲自己怎样「在两种文化之间」来回切换。

words.enDefinition: shaped by or familiar with two different cultural settings

examples.en: My classmate described herself as bicultural when she shared her family photographs.
examples.zh: 同学分享家庭照片时，说自己「受两种文化影响」。

examples.en: He said his bicultural upbringing helped him see why the two groups disagreed.
examples.zh: 他说自己「受两种文化影响的」成长经历，让他明白两组人为什么意见不合。

words.enDefinition: family origins drawn from more than one cultural or ethnic background

examples.en: The student spoke about her mixed heritage while showing us an old family map.
examples.zh: 那名学生给我们看一张旧家谱地图时，谈到了自己的「多元文化出身」。

examples.en: My friend said one label didn't fully describe his mixed heritage.
examples.zh: 朋友说，用一个标签说不清他的「多元文化出身」。

words.enDefinition: cultural influences inherited from one's family or community

examples.en: The recording project encouraged my classmates to talk about their cultural roots.
examples.zh: 这个录音项目鼓励同学谈谈自己的「文化根脉」。

examples.en: I learned more about my cultural roots when my uncle explained the song.
examples.zh: 舅舅解释那首歌后，我对自己的「文化根脉」了解得更多了。

words.enDefinition: a family or community language passed down where another language is dominant

examples.en: She takes weekend classes to keep learning her heritage language while studying abroad.
examples.zh: 留学期间，她周末上课继续学自己的「传承语」。

examples.en: I heard my heritage language at the community market near the student residence.
examples.zh: 我在学生宿舍附近的社区市场听到了自己的「传承语」。

words.enDefinition: someone raised with a family or community language in a different dominant language setting

examples.en: The workshop welcomed each heritage speaker to talk about what they could already do.
examples.zh: 工作坊请每位「传承语使用者」说说自己已经能用这门语言做些什么。

examples.en: My friend identifies as a heritage speaker even though he reads slowly.
examples.zh: 朋友虽然读得比较慢，还是认同自己是「传承语使用者」。

words.enDefinition: a language a person or family regularly uses at home

examples.en: My cousin and I switched to our home language when we called.
examples.zh: 我和表亲打电话时换回了「家中使用的语言」。

examples.en: The project let each student read a short passage in their home language.
examples.zh: 这个项目让每个同学用「家中使用的语言」朗读一小段。

words.enDefinition: a home where different languages are used in everyday life

examples.en: My roommate grew up in a multilingual household and uses three languages with relatives.
examples.zh: 室友在「多语言家庭」长大，跟亲戚交流时用三种语言。

examples.en: In her multilingual household, family games often used words from two different languages.
examples.zh: 她在「多语言家庭」里玩全家游戏时，经常会用到两种语言的词。

collocations: grow up in a multilingual household

words.enDefinition: a language someone learns in addition to the ones they already use

examples.en: I use an additional language for classes and my first language at home.
examples.zh: 我上课用「另外学的一门语言」，在家用第一语言。

examples.en: The student wrote about making friends while studying in an additional language.
examples.zh: 那名学生写了自己用「另外学的一门语言」上课时交朋友的经历。

words.enDefinition: switching between languages or language varieties in a conversation

examples.en: My classmate used code-switching when quoting her aunt's words during the interview.
examples.zh: 访谈中，同学引用姨妈的话时用了「语码转换」。

examples.en: We noticed code-switching in the recording after the speaker changed to a local dialect.
examples.zh: 发言者转用当地方言后，我们从录音中听出了「语码转换」。

words.enDefinition: how comfortable a person feels using a particular language

examples.en: My language confidence grew once I joined a group that met every Friday.
examples.zh: 加入每周五见面的一个小组后，我「使用这门语言的自信」慢慢增加了。

examples.en: My friend said she gained language confidence by trying short conversations at the market.
examples.zh: 朋友说，在市场试着跟人简单聊几句，提升了她「使用这门语言的自信」。

words.expression: keep up with a fast conversation
words.lemma: keep up with a fast conversation
words.enDefinition: to follow what people say when they speak quickly
acceptedEnVariants: keep up with a fast conversation

examples.en: I couldn't keep up with a fast conversation over lunch that first week.
examples.zh: 第一周午餐时，我没法「跟上语速快的谈话」。

examples.en: It took me a while to keep up with a fast conversation in English.
examples.zh: 过了好一阵，我才能「跟上语速很快的英语谈话」。

collocations: struggle to keep up with a fast conversation
try to keep up with a fast conversation
learn to keep up with a fast conversation

words.enDefinition: to mentally convert between languages while listening or preparing to speak

examples.en: I still translate in my head when I hear an unfamiliar expression.
examples.zh: 听到不熟悉的说法时，我还是会「在心里先翻译」。

examples.en: “Do you translate in your head?” my classmate asked after the discussion.
examples.zh: 讨论结束后，同学问「你会在心里先翻译吗？」

collocations: tend to translate in your head
no longer need to translate in your head
translate in your head while listening

words.expression: join in at your own pace
words.lemma: join in at your own pace
words.enDefinition: to start participating gradually as you become comfortable
acceptedEnVariants: join in at your own pace

examples.en: The workshop host said you could join in at your own pace.
examples.zh: 工作坊主持人说，大家可以「按自己的节奏参与」。

examples.en: “You can join in at your own pace,” my neighbour said during the game.
examples.zh: 邻居告诉我，玩游戏时可以「按自己的节奏参与」。

collocations: be free to join in at your own pace
feel welcome to join in at your own pace
leave room to join in at your own pace

words.expression: belong in more than one place
words.lemma: belong in more than one place
words.zhGloss: 在不止一个地方有归属感
words.enDefinition: to feel connected to several different places at once
acceptedZhAnswers: 在不止一个地方有归属感
acceptedEnVariants: belong in more than one place

examples.en: My classmate said she could belong in more than one place at once.
examples.zh: 同学说，她可以同时「在不止一个地方有归属感」。

examples.en: I started to believe I could belong in more than one place.
examples.zh: 我开始相信自己可以「在不止一个地方有归属感」。

collocations: feel that you belong in more than one place
learn you can belong in more than one place
understand how people belong in more than one place

words.zhGloss: 让新地方带上自己的印记
words.enDefinition: to give a place a personal feel through familiar touches and routines
acceptedZhAnswers: 让新地方带上自己的印记

examples.en: The speaker described how to make a place your own after moving abroad.
examples.zh: 发言者讲了移居国外后，怎样「让新地方带上自己的印记」。

examples.en: Small things can help you make a place your own, like arranging your favourite books.
examples.zh: 收拾摆放自己喜欢的书之类的小事，能「让新地方带上自己的印记」。

collocations: find ways to make a place your own
help someone make a place your own
make a place your own over time

words.enDefinition: to decide which familiar customs you want to continue

examples.en: Moving gave me a chance to choose what to keep from my old routine.
examples.zh: 搬家让我可以「选择旧习惯里哪些继续保留」。

examples.en: My friends said I could choose what to keep as I tried new traditions.
examples.zh: 朋友们说，我在尝试新传统的同时，也可以「选择哪些继续保留」。

collocations: take time to choose what to keep
choose what to keep from an old routine
be free to choose what to keep

words.enDefinition: to discover ordinary things that feel reassuring in a new setting

examples.en: I could find familiar comforts at the market, including snacks my aunt used to buy.
examples.zh: 在市场上我能「找到熟悉的慰藉」，包括姨妈以前常买的小吃。

examples.en: Our first shared meal helped me find familiar comforts in the unfamiliar kitchen.
examples.zh: 第一次一起做饭，帮我在陌生的厨房里「找到了熟悉的慰藉」。

collocations: look around to find familiar comforts
be glad to find familiar comforts
find familiar comforts in a new city

words.zhGloss: 重新亲近自己的文化根脉
words.enDefinition: to renew contact with traditions linked to your family or community history
acceptedZhAnswers: 重新亲近自己的文化根脉

examples.en: The speaker described how you can reconnect with your roots through family recipes.
examples.zh: 发言者讲了怎样通过家传菜谱「重新亲近自己的文化根脉」。

examples.en: The archive offers one way to reconnect with your roots through recorded family stories.
examples.zh: 档案里录下的家庭故事，是「重新亲近自己的文化根脉」的一种途径。

collocations: find ways to reconnect with your roots
use stories to reconnect with your roots
reconnect with your roots through music

words.enDefinition: an event where people present arts, practices or stories from their communities

examples.en: Our cultural showcase included recordings collected by students from their own families.
examples.zh: 我们的「文化展示活动」播放了同学们从自己家里收集的录音。

examples.en: I chose to explain a game at the cultural showcase this year.
examples.zh: 今年的「文化展示活动」上，我选择介绍一种游戏。

collocations: take part in a cultural showcase

words.enDefinition: a small stand presenting objects, stories or activities from a community

examples.en: At our cultural booth, visitors could listen to songs people grew up hearing.
examples.zh: 来我们的「文化展示摊位」，参观者可以听到不同的人从小听的歌。

examples.en: I spent an hour helping at the cultural booth near the library entrance.
examples.zh: 我在图书馆入口旁的「文化展示摊位」帮了一个小时。

words.enDefinition: a group meeting where people take turns sharing their own stories

examples.en: I spoke about moving overseas during a story circle at the library.
examples.zh: 我在图书馆的「围坐分享故事的小组」里讲了移居国外的经历。

examples.en: The story circle let everyone choose whether to tell a story or listen.
examples.zh: 这个「围坐分享故事的小组」让每个人自己选，可以讲故事，也可以听别人讲。

collocations: take part in a story circle

words.enDefinition: conversation among people with different religious or nonreligious beliefs

examples.en: The student society organised an interfaith dialogue about what people do in difficult times.
examples.zh: 学生社团组织了一场「不同信仰间的对话」，聊遇到难事时各自会怎么做。

examples.en: I attended an interfaith dialogue and listened to experiences different from my own.
examples.zh: 我参加了「不同信仰间的对话」，听到一些和我不同的经历。

collocations: take part in an interfaith dialogue

words.enDefinition: a practice or occasion followed for reasons of faith

examples.en: Our organiser asked whether the rehearsal might overlap with a religious observance.
examples.zh: 组织者问排练时间会不会与某项「宗教礼仪活动」冲突。

examples.en: My friend mentioned a religious observance when we planned the next meeting.
examples.zh: 我们安排下次见面时，朋友提到一项「宗教礼仪活动」。

collocations: take part in a religious observance

words.enDefinition: a calendar showing significant occasions across different faith traditions

examples.en: The club checked the multifaith calendar before choosing its next rehearsal date.
examples.zh: 社团先查了「多种信仰纪念日历」，才定下次排练的日期。

examples.en: I found a multifaith calendar on the noticeboard outside the common room.
examples.zh: 我在公共休息室外的公告板上找到了「多种信仰纪念日历」。

words.enDefinition: a quiet area for personal thought, prayer or contemplation

examples.en: The building map showed a reflection space near the ground-floor meeting rooms.
examples.zh: 建筑导览图标出底层会议室旁有一个「静思空间」。

examples.en: I asked the event organiser whether the reflection space would remain open after lunch.
examples.zh: 我问活动组织者，午饭后「静思空间」是否还开放。

words.enDefinition: a practical session for exploring different cultural perspectives or practices

examples.en: Our intercultural workshop began with two students showing how their families made tea.
examples.zh: 我们的「跨文化工作坊」一开始，两名同学演示了各自家里怎么泡茶。

examples.en: I brought an object from home to the intercultural workshop on Thursday.
examples.zh: 周四去「跨文化工作坊」时，我带了一件从家里拿来的物品。

words.enDefinition: shared expectations for how a group will conduct a discussion

examples.en: We agreed on discussion ground rules before sharing experiences from our hometowns.
examples.zh: 大家聊家乡经历之前，先商量了「讨论基本规则」。

examples.en: The handout put the discussion ground rules above the first group question.
examples.zh: 资料把「讨论基本规则」列在第一道小组讨论题的上面。

words.enDefinition: to welcome others expressing interpretations different from one's own

examples.en: Our chair tried to make room for different viewpoints during the discussion.
examples.zh: 讨论时，主持人尽量「给不同看法留出空间」。

examples.en: Working in pairs helped us make room for different viewpoints in the session.
examples.zh: 两人分组让我们能在活动中「给不同看法留出空间」。

collocations: try to make room for different viewpoints
learn to make room for different viewpoints
help make room for different viewpoints

words.enDefinition: to choose to skip a question instead of answering it

examples.en: The facilitator said we could pass on a question about family experience.
examples.zh: 引导员说，涉及家庭经历的问题，大家可以「选择不回答」。

examples.en: I chose to pass on a question about a lesson from childhood.
examples.zh: 我对那个关于童年经验的问题「选择不作答」。

collocations: feel free to pass on a question
choose to pass on a question
allow participants to pass on a question

words.enDefinition: to speak or act on behalf of everyone with a given cultural background

examples.en: Nobody expected me to represent an entire culture when I shared a story.
examples.zh: 我讲自己的故事时，没人指望我「代表整个文化群体」。

examples.en: She explained why one student couldn't represent an entire culture in the discussion.
examples.zh: 她解释了为什么一个学生在讨论中无法「代表整个文化群体」。

collocations: be asked to represent an entire culture
feel pressure to represent an entire culture
expect someone to represent an entire culture

words.zhGloss: 对某一文化的刻板印象
words.enDefinition: an oversimplified belief about people associated with a particular culture
acceptedZhAnswers: 对某一文化的刻板印象

examples.en: The class discussed why the film's joke depended on a cultural stereotype.
examples.zh: 全班讨论了为什么电影里的笑话建立在「对某一文化的刻板印象」上。

examples.en: My classmate challenged a cultural stereotype by describing her own mixed experiences.
examples.zh: 同学讲了自己的多种经历，对「有关某一文化的刻板印象」提出了质疑。

words.enDefinition: to draw a broad conclusion based on one case alone

examples.en: The tutor asked us not to generalise from one example about family traditions.
examples.zh: 导师请我们别根据一个家庭传统的例子「以偏概全」。

examples.en: I tried not to generalise from one example in our campus interviews.
examples.zh: 我尽量不从校园访谈的一个例子「以偏概全」。

collocations: be careful not to generalise from one example
easy to generalise from one example

words.enDefinition: students with varied personal, social or cultural experiences

examples.en: The project paired students from different backgrounds to prepare a short audio guide.
examples.zh: 项目让「不同背景的学生」两人一组，制作简短的语音导览。

examples.en: We asked students from different backgrounds which examples belonged in the display.
examples.zh: 我们问了几位「不同背景的学生」，哪些例子适合放到展板上。

collocations: bring together students from different backgrounds
hear from students from different backgrounds

words.enDefinition: a printed or digital document giving event information in two languages

examples.en: The bilingual handout helped my friend check how the game was played.
examples.zh: 「双语讲义」帮朋友看懂这个游戏是怎么玩的。

examples.en: I used the bilingual handout to follow the discussion with my classmate.
examples.zh: 我用「双语讲义」和同学一起跟上了讨论。

words.enDefinition: event information rewritten in another language for participants

examples.en: The committee made translated event materials available at the welcome desk.
examples.zh: 委员会把「翻译后的活动资料」放在了迎宾台。

examples.en: I helped a visitor find the translated event materials on the shared site.
examples.zh: 我帮一位访客在共享网站上找到了「翻译后的活动资料」。

collocations: offer translated event materials in several languages

words.enDefinition: to form small groups containing people from different backgrounds or teams

examples.en: We were asked to break into mixed groups with students from other clubs.
examples.zh: 我们被请去和其他社团的同学「分成背景多样的小组」。

examples.en: The organiser invited us to break into mixed groups for the story exercise.
examples.zh: 组织者邀请我们「分成背景多样的小组」，做讲故事的练习。

collocations: ask people to break into mixed groups
agree to break into mixed groups
break into mixed groups for a discussion

words.enDefinition: to decide what amount of personal information to tell others

examples.en: The session leader said we could choose how much to share in the group.
examples.zh: 活动负责人说，在小组里可以「自己决定分享多少」。

examples.en: I liked being able to choose how much to share during the exercise.
examples.zh: 我喜欢在练习中能「自己决定分享多少」。

collocations: let people choose how much to share
feel free to choose how much to share
allow everyone to choose how much to share

words.enDefinition: to participate using a way besides speaking aloud

examples.en: We could take part without speaking by pointing to pictures on our cards.
examples.zh: 我们可以指卡片上的图，「不用发言也能参与」。

examples.en: I was glad I could take part without speaking during the first meeting.
examples.zh: 第一次开会时，我很高兴可以「不用发言也能参与」。

collocations: choose to take part without speaking
let visitors take part without speaking

words.zhGloss: 包容不同参与者的活动
words.enDefinition: an event planned so people with varied needs or backgrounds can participate
acceptedZhAnswers: 包容不同参与者的活动

examples.en: We wanted an inclusive event where students could bring different parts of themselves.
examples.zh: 我们想办一场「包容不同参与者的活动」，让同学们能自在展现自己的不同面向。

examples.en: The group asked attendees what would make it feel like an inclusive event.
examples.zh: 小组问出席者，怎样才会让他们觉得这是一场「包容不同参与者的活动」。

collocations: help make an inclusive event welcoming

words.zhGloss: 给少发言的人表达的机会
words.enDefinition: to help people who speak less often contribute to a discussion
acceptedZhAnswers: 给少发言的人表达的机会

examples.en: Our moderator paused after each question to make space for quieter voices.
examples.zh: 主持人每问一个问题后就停一停，「给少发言的人表达的机会」。

examples.en: Writing before sharing helped us make space for quieter voices in our team.
examples.zh: 先写下来再分享，帮我们「给小组里少发言的人表达的机会」。

collocations: try to make space for quieter voices
take time to make space for quieter voices
find ways to make space for quieter voices

words.enDefinition: to alternate translating what people say during a conversation

examples.en: Our bilingual volunteers agreed to take turns interpreting during the informal game.
examples.zh: 双语志愿者约好，在这场非正式游戏中「轮流做口译」。

examples.en: We decided to take turns interpreting while our relatives shared memories on a call.
examples.zh: 亲戚们在通话中分享回忆时，我们决定「轮流做口译」。

collocations: ask volunteers to take turns interpreting
take turns interpreting during an exchange

words.enDefinition: to feel that others acknowledge who you are or what you experience

examples.en: Hearing a story like mine helped me feel seen at the gathering.
examples.zh: 聚会上有人讲的经历跟我的类似，让我「觉得自己被看见」。

examples.en: My classmate said she began to feel seen when our group mentioned her language.
examples.zh: 同学说，小组提到她使用的语言时，她开始「觉得自己被看见」。

words.expression: open to people from all backgrounds
words.lemma: open to people from all backgrounds
words.zhGloss: 欢迎不同背景的人参与
words.enDefinition: welcoming participants regardless of their personal or cultural background
acceptedZhAnswers: 欢迎不同背景的人参与
acceptedEnVariants: open to people from all backgrounds

examples.en: The poster said the story night was open to people from all backgrounds this year.
examples.zh: 海报写着，今年的故事分享夜「欢迎不同背景的人参与」。

examples.en: I joined after learning that the discussion was open to people from all backgrounds.
examples.zh: 我得知这次讨论「欢迎不同背景的人参与」，便加入了。

collocations: an event open to people from all backgrounds
a group open to people from all backgrounds
make an event open to people from all backgrounds

words.zhGloss: 把每个人看作独立个体
words.enDefinition: to respond to the person rather than assume they represent a group
acceptedZhAnswers: 把每个人看作独立个体

examples.en: The tutor encouraged us to treat people as individuals in our interview project.
examples.zh: 导师鼓励我们，在访谈项目里「把每个人看作独立个体」。

examples.en: The meeting was easier once we tried to treat people as individuals.
examples.zh: 我们试着「把每个人看作独立个体」后，会议聊得顺畅多了。

collocations: remember to treat people as individuals
try to treat people as individuals
learn to treat people as individuals

words.enDefinition: a local organisation working with a group on a shared project

examples.en: A community partner helped our class put together an exhibition about local stories.
examples.zh: 一家「社区合作方」帮我们班策划了一个关于当地故事的展览。

examples.en: I met the community partner at the public library before the workshop.
examples.zh: 工作坊开始前，我在公共图书馆见了「社区合作方」。

words.enDefinition: to organise and run an event together with another person or group

examples.en: The language clubs agreed to co-host an event for anyone interested in storytelling.
examples.zh: 几个语言社团约好「共同主办活动」，欢迎对讲故事感兴趣的人参加。

examples.en: Our society offered to co-host an event with the neighbourhood arts group.
examples.zh: 我们社团提出和社区艺术团体「共同主办一场活动」。

collocations: co-host an event with another group

words.enDefinition: a group whose participants use different languages

examples.en: I joined a mixed-language group to make captions for a local history video.
examples.zh: 我加入了一个「使用不同语言的小组」，给一段地方历史视频做字幕。

examples.en: Our mixed-language group wrote questions in whichever languages we felt comfortable using.
examples.zh: 我们这个「使用不同语言的小组」用各自熟悉的语言写了问题。

collocations: a conversation in a mixed-language group

words.enDefinition: a way to take part by writing a reply without speaking aloud

examples.en: The workshop had a written response option for anyone who preferred taking notes.
examples.zh: 工作坊为更愿意写的人提供了「书面回应选项」。

examples.en: I used the written response option to add a story after the discussion.
examples.zh: 讨论结束后，我用了「书面回应选项」，补充了一个故事。

words.enDefinition: to signal that others are free to ask about something unfamiliar

examples.en: Our speakers said they would welcome questions about the traditions they had described.
examples.zh: 发言者说，关于他们介绍的传统，「欢迎大家提问」。

examples.en: We wanted to welcome questions from people who had not played the game.
examples.zh: 我们想让没玩过这个游戏的人知道，这里「欢迎大家提问」。

words.enDefinition: to ask questions that invite fuller answers than yes or no

examples.en: Our tutor encouraged us to ask open-ended questions during the cultural exchange interviews.
examples.zh: 导师鼓励我们在文化交流访谈中「问开放式问题」。

examples.en: The host took time to ask open-ended questions about how the custom had changed.
examples.zh: 主持人花时间就习俗如何演变「问了开放式问题」。

collocations: encourage people to ask open-ended questions
